title: Practice mode
body: Solve the support reactions step by step.

steps.title: Identify support reactions
steps.goal: Select all unknown support reactions that belong in the free-body diagram.

feedback.correct: Correct. The pin at A gives A_x and A_y, and the roller at B gives B_y.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Check which motions each support can prevent.

mistakes.text: A pin support cannot transmit a support moment.
A roller support does not create a horizontal reaction.
A roller support cannot transmit a moment.
The pin support at A can prevent horizontal motion, so A_x is an unknown.
The pin support at A can prevent vertical motion, so A_y is an unknown.
The roller support at B creates a vertical reaction B_y.

hints.text: A pin support has two force components.
A roller support has one reaction normal to the surface.
Neither support in this problem is a fixed support, so no support moment appears.

steps.title: Choose a moment point
steps.goal: Click the point in the canvas that makes the moment equation solve B_y directly.
steps.instructions: Use the canvas selection marker, then check your choice.

feedback.correct: Correct. Around A, A_x and A_y have zero lever arm, so the equation solves B_y directly.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Choose a point that removes as many unknown reactions as possible from the moment equation.

mistakes.text: The midpoint is possible, but not ideal: F would disappear and both support reactions remain.
Point B is possible, but it solves A_y first. Point A solves B_y directly.
Use point A so the reactions at A have zero lever arm.

hints.text: A force through the moment point creates no moment.
Taking moments about A removes both A_x and A_y.
With moments about A, only F and B_y remain in the equation.

steps.title: Match lever arms around A
steps.goal: Match each force to its perpendicular lever arm about point A.

feedback.correct: Correct. The reactions at A have zero lever arm, F acts at L/2, and B_y acts at L.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Measure every lever arm from point A to the force line of action.

mistakes.text: A_x acts at A, so its lever arm around A is zero.
A_y acts at A, so its lever arm around A is zero.
F is applied at the middle, so its lever arm is L/2.
B_y acts at B, so its lever arm from A is L.
A_x acts at A, so its lever arm around A is zero.
A_y acts at A, so its lever arm around A is zero.
F is applied at the middle, so its lever arm is L/2.
B_y acts at B, so its lever arm from A is L.

hints.text: The lever arm is the distance from A to the force line of action.
Forces applied exactly at A have no moment about A.
The load is centered, while support B is one full span away from A.

steps.title: Determine moment signs
steps.goal: Use counterclockwise positive and match each term to its sign.

feedback.correct: Correct. B_y rotates counterclockwise about A, while F rotates clockwise.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Apply the sign convention: counterclockwise moments are positive.

mistakes.text: B_y at B rotates counterclockwise around A, therefore it is positive.
F in the middle rotates clockwise around A, therefore it is negative.
B_y at B rotates counterclockwise around A, therefore it is positive.
F in the middle rotates clockwise around A, therefore it is negative.

hints.text: Imagine the beam rotating about A.
An upward force at B lifts the right end and turns the beam counterclockwise.
The downward load in the middle pushes the right side down and turns the beam clockwise.

steps.title: Build the moment equation
steps.goal: Choose the terms for the moment equilibrium equation about A.

feedback.correct: Correct. The moment equation is B_y · L - F · L/2 = 0.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Keep only the nonzero moment terms about A, with signs from the chosen convention.

mistakes.text: Missing B_y · L: B_y creates a moment around A.
Missing -F · L/2: F creates a moment around A.
Wrong sign for F: F rotates clockwise around A and is negative.
Wrong sign for B_y: B_y rotates counterclockwise around A and is positive.
Use F · L/2, not F · L, because the load is at the middle.
A_y acts at point A, so its lever arm around A is zero and the term should be omitted.
A_x acts at point A, so its lever arm around A is zero and the term should be omitted.

hints.text: Only F and B_y have nonzero lever arms about A.
B_y is positive and F is negative with counterclockwise positive.
The equation has the form B_y · L - F · L/2 = 0.

steps.title: Solve for B_y
steps.goal: Solve the moment equation for B_y.
steps.instructions: Use the equilibrium equation from the previous step: ΣM_A = B_y · L - F · L/2 = 0.

feedback.correct: Correct. B_y carries half of the centered load.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Start from B_y · L - F · L/2 = 0 and isolate B_y.

mistakes.text: B_y = F means you forgot that the lever arm of F is L/2.
B_y is a force; after dividing the moment equation by L, no L remains.
A negative result means one moment sign was reversed.
Divide both sides by L after moving F · L/2 to the other side.

hints.text: Move F · L/2 to the right side.
Then divide the whole equation by L.
The L cancels, leaving B_y = F/2.

steps.title: Build the vertical force equation
steps.goal: Choose the terms for vertical force equilibrium.

feedback.correct: Correct. The vertical equilibrium equation is A_y + B_y - F = 0.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Only vertical forces belong in ΣF_y, and upward is positive.

mistakes.text: Missing A_y: the vertical reaction at A contributes to ΣF_y.
Missing B_y: the vertical reaction at B contributes to ΣF_y.
Missing -F: the external force points downward.
F points downward, so it enters the vertical equilibrium equation with a negative sign.
A_x is horizontal and does not belong in vertical equilibrium.

hints.text: Use y positive upward.
Both support reactions point upward, while F points downward.
The equation should be A_y + B_y - F = 0.

steps.title: Solve for A_y
steps.goal: Use B_y = F/2 in vertical equilibrium and solve for A_y.
steps.instructions: Use the equilibrium equation from the previous step: ΣF_y = A_y + B_y - F = 0.

feedback.correct: Correct. A_y also carries half of the load.
feedback.genericIncorrect: Insert B_y = F/2 into A_y + B_y - F = 0.

mistakes.text: A_y = F ignores that B_y already carries half of the load.
A_y cannot be zero; vertical equilibrium requires both supports to balance F.
A_y points upward in the chosen direction, so it is positive.
From A_y + F/2 - F = 0, the remaining reaction is F/2.

hints.text: Substitute B_y = F/2.
Move F/2 to the right side to get A_y = F/2.

steps.title: Final equilibrium check
steps.goal: Choose the statement that verifies all equilibrium equations.

options.label: ΣF_x = 0, ΣF_y = F/2 + F/2 - F = 0, and ΣM_A = F/2 · L - F · L/2 = 0.
Only ΣF_y has to be checked because the beam is horizontal.
Only ΣM_A has to be checked because it gave B_y.

feedback.correct: The solution satisfies all equilibrium equations. Because the problem is symmetric, both vertical support reactions carry half of the load.
feedback.genericIncorrect: A statics solution must satisfy force equilibrium and moment equilibrium.

mistakes.text: Vertical force equilibrium is necessary, but moment equilibrium must also be satisfied.
Moment equilibrium is necessary, but force equilibrium must also be satisfied.

hints.text: Check every independent equilibrium equation.
There is no horizontal external load, so A_x = 0 satisfies ΣF_x.
The two vertical reactions add to F, and their moment about A balances the load moment.
